original_test_intent: Read one verified sensor's all-event-message state, scanning state and any returned individual assertion/deassertion enable masks over OOB without changing monitoring policy.
original_method: Preserve Master TBD; Review maps the title to IPMI v2.0 Table 35-11 raw 0x04/0x29 <sensor number> and its permitted variable-length response.
manual_activity: Project supplies the sensor number, matched SDR event-control capability and expected monitoring state; no write approval is required for the read.
required_inputs: Matched SDR and Sensor Event Message Control Support
safety_requirements: Never guess the sensor number or event type
Accept only the protocol-permitted 2-to-6-byte response shape
Do not issue 0x28, PEF or event receiver writes
agent_execution_scope: Bind the sensor number to one SDR and event-reading type
Validate completion, all-event-message bit, scanning bit and conditional response length
Decode only returned assertion/deassertion mask bytes using threshold or discrete semantics
Compare the state with the SDR capability and approved monitoring baseline
Archive raw and decoded no-mutation evidence
engineer_actions: Approve sensor mapping and expected monitoring state
Review unsupported or contradictory capability states

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: DeepSeek is safe but overly restrictive: after sensor mapping, the standard 0x04/0x29 read is deterministic and does not need mutation approval.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use one secret-safe raw 0x04 0x29 <sensor number> request as defined by IPMI v2.0 Table 35-11; parse the all-event-message and scanning bits, then decode any returned assertion/deassertion masks according to the matched SDR and permitted 2-to-6-byte response.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: No Master command or sensor is invented; source TBD and 10/5 timing remain unchanged.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Perform one sensor-bound read, validate the response length conditionally, decode global/scanning state separately from individual masks and compare the result with SDR capability and monitoring policy.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds a conditional standard read in the Review layer while preserving the original TBD state.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: This does not prove 0x28 write behavior, event delivery under stimulus, PEF routing, event receiver configuration or SEL logging.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: When all event messages are disabled, omitted mask bytes are valid and must not be reported as truncation; unsupported per-event control cannot be inferred from zeros.

project_override_considerations: A high-level API is equivalent only if it exposes the same sensor identity, all-event-message and scanning states, individual masks when supported, and the distinction between unavailable and zero.
expected_evidence: Completion, response length and global/scanning bits
Decoded assertion/deassertion masks with event-type mapping

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The title consistently identifies Get Sensor Event Enable while Procedure and Criteria are TBD. Missing command, parsing and acceptance semantics plus generic log clearing are source omissions rather than contradictory source requirements; the Review mapping remains conditional and preserves Master TBD.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The read function and response schema are defined. Sensor mapping, SDR capability and expected state are normal Project readiness inputs; unsupported or malformed results must be reported without guessing.

review_improvement: Handles the protocol's conditional response length and distinguishes global event-message disable, scanning disable and individual mask state rather than interpreting absent bytes as zero.
independent_technical_reasoning: Table 35-11 permits two through six response bytes and allows individual mask bytes to be omitted when all event messages are disabled. The parser must first interpret the global/scanning status and SDR capability, then decide which mask bytes are meaningful. A fixed-length assumption would falsely label a valid disabled state as truncation or fabricate zero masks.
